notes: Five inverting-style op-amp stages, drawn rotated 90deg (all triangles have their flat input edge on TOP, '+' at the left end of that edge, '-' at the right end, apex/output pointing DOWN). Sources are at the top; a common rail runs across the bottom. Net map: 0 = the ground node, shared by all six GND symbols (15, 16, 17, 18, 21, 23) and everything they touch: GND 15 -> left terminal of I-DC 4; GND 17 -> left terminal of V-DC 1; GND 23 -> in+ of Op-Amp 22; GND 21 -> in+ of Op-Amp 19; GND 18 -> in+ of Op-Amp 20; GND 16 -> in+ of Op-Amp 13. n1 = right terminal of I-DC 4 -> right to x~211 -> down to the in- of Op-Amp 22, with a T at (211,118) branching right to x~238 and down into the TOP of Inductor 12. n2 = output of Op-Amp 22 (apex at (199,203)) -> down -> right at y~232 to x~235, joining the BOTTOM of Inductor 12, then the long vertical at x~235 all the way down to the TOP of Resistor 7. n3 = right terminal of V-DC 1 -> right to x~441 -> down to the in- of Op-Amp 19, with a T at (441,88) branching right to x~480 and down into the TOP plate of Capacitor 9. n4 = output of Op-Amp 19 (apex at (418,187)) -> down to y~222 -> right to x~482 -> up to the BOTTOM plate of Capacitor 9; the same output column continues down to the TOP of Resistor 11. n5 = the long horizontal at y~288..296: TOP plate of Capacitor 2 at (68,297) -> right across the whole drawing to (353,282) -> down to y~370 -> right to x~400 -> down into the in+ of Op-Amp 0. Only two terminals. n6 = BOTTOM plate of Capacitor 2 -> down x~68 to the in- of Op-Amp 20, with a T at (68,345) branching right to x~102 and down into the TOP of Inductor 3. n7 = output of Op-Amp 20 (apex at (62,423)) -> right at y~431 to the BOTTOM of Inductor 3; same node continues down into the TOP of Resistor 10. n8 = BOTTOM of Resistor 7 -> down x~236 to the in- of Op-Amp 13, with a T at (236,383) branching right to x~292 and down into the TOP plate of Capacitor 6. n9 = output of Op-Amp 13 (apex at (227,449)) -> the shallow sloping wire right/up to (294,442) -> up to the BOTTOM plate of Capacitor 6; same node continues down into the TOP of Resistor 8. n10 = BOTTOM of Resistor 11 -> down x~422 to the in- of Op-Amp 0, with a T at (422,340) branching right to x~468 and down into the TOP of Inductor 5. n11 = output of Op-Amp 0 (apex at (411,436)) -> right at y~436 to the BOTTOM of Inductor 5; same node continues down into the TOP of Resistor 14. n12 = the bottom rail at y~490..494, running from x~60 to x~412 and holding exactly three terminals: BOTTOM of Resistor 10 (left end), BOTTOM of Resistor 8 (T up at x~229) and BOTTOM of Resistor 14 (right end). Judgment calls: (a) THE key call -- the only wire crossing in the drawing is at (235,291), where the long horizontal n5 crosses the long vertical n2 (Op-Amp 22 output down to Resistor 7). At 20x and by direct pixel measurement both strokes are 1 px thick right through the intersection (columns 231-239 of the horizontal show only the normal 1-px y-step from 290 to 292, never a 3+ px blob), and the vertical shows no semicircular hop. No dot, no hop -> treated as a CROSSOVER, i.e. two separate nets, per the plain-X rule. Note the electrical consequence, which is why this deserves a second pair of eyes: n5 then has no driver (Capacitor 2's top plate and Op-Amp 0's in+ only), and Op-Amp 20's stage is fed only through that capacitor. If a human decides the drafter meant a junction, n2 and n5 merge into one 5-terminal net and nothing else changes. (b) The 1-2 px gap in the vertical just above the crossing (y~273) is a pen-lift/scan artifact, not a break -- the stroke resumes on exactly the same x and there is no component or node there. (c) Op-amp pin order is in+, in-, out for all five; the +/- glyphs are legible at 6x on every triangle, and in every case the in+ lead comes in from the left (GND, except Op-Amp 0 whose in+ comes from n5) while the in- lead comes down from above. (d) All two-terminal parts are drawn vertically except the two sources; index 0 = top lead / top plate, index 1 = bottom, and for I-DC 4 and V-DC 1 index 0 = left (grounded) lead, index 1 = right. Two-terminal order does not affect any metric. (e) The bottom rail n12 touches no GND symbol, so it is NOT net 0 -- it is a genuine floating three-resistor node; the six GND symbols are the only things named 0. (f) No terminal is left unconnected; every one of the 47 terminals lands on one of the 13 nets.
